concerns.text: Tasks T220–T242 (Phase 8-10) implement 'Review Response' features (explicit bond length validation, angle-aware message passing, reference error analysis against experimental data) that directly contradict the spec.md Assumptions which explicitly state 'Physical measurement validation is out of scope,' 'hydration effects are out-of-scope,' and 'ensemble sampling is documented as future work'. These tasks constitute unauthorized scope creep that violates the project's defined boundaries (FR-011, FR-010). No spec FR/SC exists to support these tasks.

Task T232 attempts to 'compute the theoretical MAE/RMSE floor by comparing QM9 DFT values against available experimental benchmarks'. This violates spec.md FR-011 and Constitution Principle II because the spec explicitly excludes physical measurement validation and the plan confirms no experimental benchmark set is available or authorized for this feature. There is no matching FR/SC for this task.

Tasks T230, T231, and T234 require generating scripts and documentation to 'quantify error margins of that reference [experimental]' and 'perturb DFT values... simulating experimental noise'. This implies a validation protocol against physical reality that the spec explicitly forbids in Assumptions ('Physical measurement validation is out of scope'). No spec FR/SC supports these tasks.

Task T223 ('Implement a stereoisomer stress test... to verify 3D geometry sensitivity') introduces specific chemical validation steps not requested in spec.md FR-007 or FR-009 (which only require general feature attribution and visualization). This risks implementation of unrequested domain-specific logic that conflicts with the 'lightweight' constraint in FR-004. No spec FR/SC supports this specific stress test.

Task T220 ('flagging C-N... bonds for validation against Pauling constants') introduces specific chemical validation steps not requested in spec.md FR-002 or FR-007. The spec requires extraction of coordinates and connectivity, not validation against specific Pauling constants. No spec FR/SC supports this specific validation logic.

Task T221 ('Update feature_set.schema.yaml... to include a physical_constants feature vector') adds a new data schema element not defined in spec.md FR-003 (which only lists Morgan fingerprints and Coulomb matrices). This is an unauthorized scope expansion. No spec FR/SC supports this schema change.

Task T222 ('Modify schnet_gnn.py to incorporate an explicit angle-aware message passing layer') modifies the model architecture beyond the 'lightweight SchNet-style GNN' defined in FR-004. The spec does not mandate angle-aware layers or hybridization weighting. No spec FR/SC supports this architectural change.

Task T224 ('Extend visualize_features.py to generate heatmaps specifically highlighting... bond angles and electronegativity differences') adds specific visualization requirements not found in FR-009 (which only requires 'visualize feature importance maps'). No spec FR/SC supports this specific heatmap requirement.

Task T240 ('Enhance saliency_mapping.py to specifically visualize the gradient with respect to atomic partial charges') adds a specific visualization requirement not found in FR-007 (which only requires 'saliency mapping to GNN node embeddings'). No spec FR/SC supports this specific gradient visualization.

Task T242 ('Implement a Vector Sum Check... comparing the model's predicted dipole vector against a simple vector sum of bond dipoles') introduces a new validation metric not defined in spec.md FR-006 or FR-008. No spec FR/SC supports this specific vector sum check.

Task T241 ('Update research.md to discuss the Physics-Informed aspect...') requires documenting architectural constraints not mandated by the spec. While documentation is good, the specific content (physics-informed loss discussion) implies features (physics-informed loss) that are explicitly out of scope per spec assumptions. No spec FR/SC supports this specific documentation requirement.

Task T233 ('Update research.md to clarify the distinction between computational prediction and experimental measurement') is a documentation task that implies a validation protocol against physical reality which is out of scope. While clarifying limitations is good, the specific requirement to 'explicitly state that the model predicts DFT values, not physical reality' in the context of a 'Review Response' phase suggests a scope creep in the validation narrative. No spec FR/SC explicitly mandates this specific phrasing as a task.

Task T225 ('Update research.md to document the specific physical constants used...') requires documenting constants and constraints not mandated by the spec. The spec requires validation against QM9 DFT data, not against Pauling constants. No spec FR/SC supports this specific documentation requirement.

Task T230 ('Update research.md to include a dedicated Validation Protocol section... explicitly stating the known error margin of these calculations compared to experimental values') requires quantifying error margins against experimental values, which is explicitly out of scope per spec.md Assumptions. No spec FR/SC supports this task.

Task T231 ('Add a Hydration & Conformational Limitations section... explicitly stating that hydration effects... are out-of-scope') is a documentation task. While acknowledging limitations is good, the task is part of a 'Review Response' phase that implies a need to address concerns about hydration effects which are out of scope. The spec already lists these as assumptions. No new spec FR/SC is needed, but the task implies a scope creep in the validation narrative.

Task T234 ('Add a task to statistical_tests.py to perform a sensitivity analysis on the reference data... simulating experimental noise') introduces a new statistical test not defined in FR-008 (which only requires paired t-tests). No spec FR/SC supports this specific sensitivity analysis.
